title: design-pages.json
description: Opt-in configuration for @design-parity/page-backdrop. The feature is off unless this file exists AND sets "enabled": true.

enabled.description: Page backdrops run only when this is exactly true. Any other value — including omitting the field — leaves the feature off, so the configuration can be committed and reviewed before it is switched on. Required here so the choice is always stated explicitly rather than inherited from a default.

source.description: Design source. Only Figma exposes a page-level read API today.

fileKey.description: Figma file key — the segment after /design/ in the file URL.

pages.description: The key pages to import, in priority order. Explicit by design: nothing is auto-discovered.

nodeId.description: Node id of the page frame, e.g. "1:2" (a figma.com URL spells it "1-2").

id.description: Slug for the page's manifest entry and PNG filename. Defaults to a slug of the frame's own name.

scale.description: PNG export scale for the backdrop images.

nested.description: Also record component instances nested inside another instance. Off by default: the outermost instance is the meaningful placement.

outDir.description: Where the manifest and backdrop PNGs are written, relative to this file.

overlay.description: Viewer defaults for the layer that shows code renders on top of the design.

enabled.description: Whether the overlay starts on when a page is opened. Off by default — the design is what you should see first.

blend.description: "difference" makes matching pixels black, so drift lights up.
